questions.prompt: A React external-store adapter returns a newly allocated object from `getSnapshot` on every call, even when nothing changed. What should be corrected?

choices.text: Return a fresh wrapper on every read.
Read the store only inside an Effect and omit getSnapshot altogether.
Cache snapshots until the store changes.
Mutate the last snapshot object in place while preserving its identity.

questions.explanation: React compares snapshots with Object.is. A fresh object on every read can cause repeated renders; a mutable store needs a cached immutable snapshot.

sources.title: useSyncExternalStore – React
sources.claim: useSyncExternalStore requires cached immutable snapshots until the store changes and an unsubscribe-returning subscribe function.

questions.prompt: A React search page defers the query used by an expensive result list with useDeferredValue. What does this API guarantee about request debouncing?

choices.text: A fixed half-second request debounce.
It merges all pending network requests into one HTTP request automatically.
It prevents every request until the user stops typing for one event-loop turn.
It supplies no request debounce.

questions.explanation: Deferring rendering has no fixed debounce interval and does not prevent network requests per keystroke. Request scheduling needs its own policy.

sources.title: useDeferredValue – React
sources.claim: useDeferredValue lets background rendering lag without a fixed delay and does not itself reduce network requests.

questions.prompt: A React 19.2 app uses useTransition for expensive view changes. Which constraints apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A transition cannot be used to control a text input.
A state setter after await currently needs another startTransition to mark it.
startTransition postpones calling its callback until the browser becomes idle.
Every state setter anywhere in the process becomes a transition until commit.
Transition updates can be interrupted by more urgent updates.

questions.explanation: A is correct: the text input value must update synchronously. B is correct: the async boundary requires wrapping those state updates again. C is incorrect: React calls the supplied action immediately. D is incorrect: transition marking is scoped to the supported action update context. E is correct: React can restart non-blocking rendering after urgent work.

sources.title: useTransition – React
sources.claim: In React 19.2, transition updates are non-blocking, cannot control text inputs, and state updates after await need another startTransition.

questions.prompt: An external React store listener is registered by `subscribe` passed to useSyncExternalStore. What should subscribe return?

choices.text: A function that removes the listener.
The current snapshot object.
A promise that resolves only after the component permanently unmounts.
The last rendered JSX element so React can skip future subscriptions.

questions.explanation: subscribe must return cleanup that unsubscribes the callback. Snapshot reading belongs in getSnapshot; JSX and a lifetime promise are not unsubscribe functions.

sources.title: useSyncExternalStore – React
sources.claim: useSyncExternalStore requires cached immutable snapshots until the store changes and an unsubscribe-returning subscribe function.

questions.prompt: A user types while React is rendering a deferred result list. How can React handle the unfinished background render?

choices.text: Finish it before handling newer input.
Interrupt it for the newer input.
Commit every obsolete result in order before displaying the latest result.
Freeze the input value until all deferred renders have completed together.

questions.explanation: Deferred rendering is interruptible. React can prioritize input and restart background work with the newer value rather than commit every obsolete render.

sources.title: useDeferredValue – React
sources.claim: useDeferredValue lets background rendering lag without a fixed delay and does not itself reduce network requests.

questions.prompt: A React 19.2 developer replaces a timer with startTransition and expects input updates to become delayed. Which observations are valid? Select all that apply.

choices.text: An update inside a later setTimeout is automatically marked by the earlier call.
A transition prevents React from interrupting an expensive render.
The action passed to startTransition runs immediately.
A controlled input should use an urgent state update for its value.
startTransition is a debounce with a fixed waiting interval.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: the setter in the timer needs its own transition wrapping. B is incorrect: non-blocking work is specifically interruptible. C is correct: non-blocking priority applies to updates, not delayed callback execution. D is correct: transition updates cannot control text inputs. E is incorrect: it schedules rendering priority without a debounce interval.

sources.title: useTransition – React
sources.claim: In React 19.2, transition updates are non-blocking, cannot control text inputs, and state updates after await need another startTransition.
